'''Stefan Marinov''' ({{langx|bg|Стефан Маринов}}) (1 February 1931 – 15 July 1997) was a [[Bulgaria]]n [[physicist]], researcher, writer, and lecturer who promoted [[Criticism of the theory of relativity|anti-relativistic theoretical viewpoints]] and later in his life defended the ideas of [[perpetual motion]] and [[Free energy suppression|free energy]]. In 1997, he self-published experimental results that confirmed [[classical electromagnetism]] and disproved that a machine he had constructed could be a source of perpetual motion.<ref name="mar1997DPa"/><ref name="mar1997DPb"/>

==Life and education==
Marinov was born on 1 February 1931 in [[Sofia]] to a family of intellectual [[communist]]s.<ref name="Marinov1987">
{{cite book
 |author       = Marinov S
 |title        = Eppur Si Muove: Axiomatics, Fundamentals and Experimental Verification of the Absolute Space-Time Theory
 |publisher    = East-West Publishers
 |location     = Graz
 |year         = 1987
 |url          = http://www.ptep-online.com/index_files/books.html
 |url-status   = dead
 |archive-url  = https://archive.today/20130104111420/http://www.ptep-online.com/index_files/books.html
 |archive-date = 2013-01-04
 }}
</ref>

In 1948, Marinov finished Soviet College in [[Prague]], then studied [[physics]] at the [[Czech Technical University in Prague]] and [[Sofia University]]. Marinov was an Assistant Professor of Physics from 1960 to 1974 at [[Sofia University]]. In 1966–67, 1974, and 1977, Marinov was subject to compulsory [[Psychiatry|psychiatric]] treatment in Sofia because of his [[political dissent]]. In September 1977, Marinov received a passport and successfully emigrated out of the country, moving to [[Brussels]]. In 1978, Marinov moved to [[Washington, D.C.]] Later he lived in [[Italy]] and [[Austria]]. In his later years, Marinov earned a living as a horse groom.

==Work==
One of Marinov's interests was the quest for [[Perpetual motion|free energy]] sources via the construction of toy theories (new axiomatic systems that putatively describe our physical reality) and their experimental testing against mainstream physical theories. In 1992, Marinov wrote a letter to German Federal Chancellor [[Helmut Kohl]] in support of a German company, Becocraft, that was doing research into "[[Perpetual motion|free energy]]" technologies and had recently been the target of lawsuits. In the letter, Marinov threatened to set himself on fire at the steps of the [[German parliament]] if Kohl was not willing to intervene in favor of Marinov's associates.

== Research ==

Marinov attempted to find experimental disproof of the theory of relativity by testing the speed of light in different directions using an arrangement of ''coupled mirrors'' and ''coupled shutters''.<ref name="Marinov1983">

 | author    = Stefan Marinov
 | title     = The interrupted 'rotating disc' experiment
 | journal   = [[Journal of Physics A]]
 | volume    = 16
 | issue     = 9
 | pages     = 1885–1888
 | year      = 1983
 | url       = http://www.helical-structures.org/selected_articles/interrupted_rot_disk_exp.pdf
 | bibcode   = 1983JPhA...16.1885M
 | doi       = 10.1088/0305-4470/16/9/013
 | citeseerx = 10.1.1.676.5642
 }}</ref><ref name="Marinov2007">
{{cite journal
 |author       = Marinov S
 |title        = New Measurement of the Earth's Absolute Velocity with the Help of the Coupled Shutters Experiment
 |journal      = [[Progress in Physics]]
 |volume       = 1
 |issue        = 1
 |pages        = 31–37
 |year         = 2007
 |bibcode      = 2007PrPh....3a..31M
 |url          = http://www.ptep-online.com/index_files/2007/PP-08-05.PDF
 |url-status   = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20120209042627/http://www.ptep-online.com/index_files/2007/PP-08-05.PDF
 |archive-date = 2012-02-09
 }}
</ref>  Marinov reported in 1974 that he had measured an [[anisotropy]] of the [[Speed of light|velocity of light]].<ref name="Marinov1974a">
{{cite journal
 | author = Marinov S
 | title = The velocity of light is direction dependent
 | journal = Czechoslovak Journal of Physics B
 | volume = 24
 | issue = 9
 | pages = 965–970
 | year = 1974
 | bibcode = 1974CzJPh..24..965M
 | doi=10.1007/BF01591047| s2cid = 122255034
 }}
</ref> However, Marinov's claims have not found acceptance within the scientific community despite his energetic efforts to promote his claims. Marinov planned to develop an updating of the [[General relativity|relativistic mechanics]] and [[electrodynamics]], as described in his self-published book ''Eppur si Muove''.<ref name="Marinov1987"/> Marinov succeeded in having his claims presented in numerous publications including [[peer-review]]ed [[Academic journal|journal]]s.<ref name="Marinov1972">

Marinov was involved publicly in many quarrels with [[John Maddox]], the editor of ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', who refused to print either his papers or his letters to the editor. He retaliated by securing the funds to place a full-page [[advertisement]] in ''Nature'' expressing his frustration with what he regarded as the dogmatic attitude of the establishment.<ref name="Marinov1996">
{{cite journal
 |author       = Stefan Marinov
 |title        = Annus Horribilis
 |journal      = [[Nature (journal)|Nature]]
 |volume       = 380
 |issue        = 6572
 |pages        = xiv
 |year         = 1996
 |url          = http://itis.volta.alessandria.it/episteme/ep6/ep6-marin.htm
 |doi          = 
 |url-status   = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20070211015515/http://itis.volta.alessandria.it/episteme/ep6/ep6-marin.htm
 |archive-date = 2007-02-11
 }}</ref> Marinov himself published a journal, ''Deutsche Physik'', of which he was editor-in-chief and which discussed mainly his ideas on physics.

Stefan Marinov was interested in experiments alleged to violate known physical laws.<ref name="Marinov1989">
{{cite journal
 | author = Stefan Marinov
 | title = The Intriguing ball-bearing motor
 | journal = Electronics World & Wireless World
 | publisher = Reed Business Publishing
 | volume = 
 | issue = April
 | pages = 
 | year = 1989
 | url = http://www.electricstuff.co.uk/bbmotor.html#article
 | doi=
}}</ref><ref name="Ogden1989">
{{cite journal
 | author = Frank Ogden
 | title = Great Balls of Fire!
 | journal = Electronics World & Wireless World
 | publisher = Reed Business Publishing
 | volume = 
 | issue = April
 | pages = 
 | year = 1989
 | url = http://www.electricstuff.co.uk/bbmotor.html#fire
 | doi=
}}</ref> Marinov claimed to have seen in operation and learned the secret of the so-called "Swiss ML converter" or Testatika electrical generator, another alleged perpetual motion machine, at a religious commune in Switzerland called [[Methernitha]].<ref name="NEN1997">
{{cite journal |author=Schneeberger E, Bass R |year=1997 |title=Stefan Marinov: In Memoriam: My Scientific Testament; A Strong Voice Is Missing (Last Will and Testament); Letter from Erwin Schneeberger; Letter from Dr. Robert W. Bass |url=http://www.padrak.com/ine/NEN_5_5_2.html |journal=New Energy News |volume=5 |issue=5 |pages=1–3}}
</ref> According to Marinov's account, this 500-member commune, led by religious leader Paul Baumann, met all its energy needs using this device.<ref name="NEN1997"/>

Marinov has been the editor of a five-volume encyclopedic series called "Classical Physics".  In 1993 Marinov also authored a book on electromagnetism that discoursed on his belief that mainstream scientific thought was mired in dogma and had discarded still-valid knowledge from scientific thought of previous eras. In 1997, in the last issue 21 of ''Deutsche Physik'', Marinov self-published experimental results that disproved that the ''Siberian Coliu'', which Marinov himself had constructed, is a perpetual motion machine, and where Marinov concluded that [[Ampere's law]] in electromagnetism is correct.<ref name="mar1997DPa">

}}
</ref><ref name="mar1997DPb">

== Death ==
Marinov died in [[Graz]], [[Austria]] on 15 July 1997.<ref name="NEN1997" />  He was 66 years old and was survived by his son, Marin Marinov, who at the time was a [[List of ministries of Bulgaria|vice-Minister of Industry of Bulgaria]].  The cause of death was [[suicide]].<ref name="NEN1997" /><ref name="pappas">
{{cite web |author=Pappas P |year=1997 |title=Update on Stefan Marinov's Death (E-mails by Panos Pappas) |url=http://www.padrak.com/ine/PAPPAS_SM.html |pages= |journal= |volume=}}
</ref>
